author: DTrim99
body:
This is the same one as #1127 — the Connecticut child tax rebate, $250 per child, so 2 dependents = the $500 you're seeing — and your OLR report nails exactly why it's misplaced:

> The child tax rebate is a one-time rebate of up to $750 ($250 per child, up to three children). ... Taxpayers are eligible for the full rebate if their federal adjusted gross income (AGI) for the **2021** [income tax year] ...
>
> — [2022-R-0110](https://cga.ct.gov/2022/rpt/pdf/2022-R-0110.pdf)

PolicyEngine currently books that rebate as a 2022 Connecticut non-refundable credit, so it comes off the 2022 return (siitax 1,805 instead of the ~2,305 of CT income tax on this record). The fix is already up: [PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9274](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-us/pull/9274) moves `ct_child_tax_rebate` to the 2021 eligibility year (as a refundable credit, the way Rhode Island's and New Mexico's prior-year rebates are handled), so it drops off the 2022 return. Once it lands, this record's 2022 CT tax reads ~2,305 with no rebate.

Small housekeeping note: the CT-1040 PDF in the directory is a different filer — federal AGI $13,095, CT tax 0 — not the $57,619-wage record in `txpydata.csv`. It doesn't change anything here, since the $500 rebate is right there in the emulator output, but flagging it in case the upload got crossed.

Happy to close this as a duplicate of #1127 unless you'd rather keep it open to track.
